definition: A model that assigns probabilities to sequences of words, typically based on statistical patterns like word co-occurrence frequencies, predating neural language models.
details: Statistical language models, including n-gram models, were the standard approach in NLP for decades before neural network-based language models became dominant with the rise of deep learning.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. Think of it this way: A model that assigns probabilities to sequences of words, typically based on statistical patterns like word co-occurrence frequencies, predating neural language models. And here is the clever part: Statistical language models, including n-gram models, were the standard approach in NLP for decades before neural network-based language models became dominant with the rise of deep learning. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. And that is Statistical Language Model — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
